NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular business
  hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a recording is
  available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35 (Cox) and
  Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails received
  before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 28, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR HUFF at 7:05 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Los Angeles County Fire Captain Brandon Comfort and Firefighter Specialist Russell
Pettit from Fire Station 106.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RECOGNITION OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY FIRE DEPARTMENT CAPTAIN
  BRANDON COMFORT AND FIREFIGHTER SPECIALIST RUSSELL PETTIT (FIRE
  STATION 106)

MAYOR HUFF presented certificates of recognition to the Captain Comfort and Firefighter
Specialist Pettit for their recent deployment as part of the Los Angeles County Fire
Department’s Urban Search & Rescue Team to Turkey to aid in earthquake rescue efforts.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz and Stegura

City Council Members Absent:  Zerunyan

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MARCH 2023 AS WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH

MAYOR HUFF declared March 2023 as Women’s History Month.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 4A-G AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz and Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 14, 2023

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 28, 2023
 C.  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2023

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF JANUARY 2023 & FEBRUARY 2023

  APPROVE WARRANTS 65977 THROUGH 66027 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $485,113.62 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 020423 THROUGH 020523; IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $90,925.95 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $576,039.57
  WITH PROPER AUDIT.

E.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF JANUARY 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF JANUARY 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 15, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS BOARD MEETING
  HIGHLIGHTS OF JANUARY 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE - FIRST QUARTER 2023

  COMMERCIAL: PENINSULA HERITAGE SCHOOL
  RESIDENTIAL: 28340 HIGHRIDGE ROAD

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  NON-PROFIT AND BUSINESS GRANT PROGRAM

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the business grant program
  guidelines to be implemented this fiscal year.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that it should be made clear that this is the last year
this grant program will be offered.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ stated she is grateful for how creative the City has been,
particularly through the pandemic in its efforts to support non-profits and small businesses.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE BUSINESS GRANT PROGRAM GUIDELINES TO BE
  IMPLEMENTED THIS FISCAL YEAR.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 28, 2023
   AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz and Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

B.  TASK ORDER FOR WILLDAN ENGINEERING TO PREPARE PLANS &
  SPECIFICATIONS, BIDDING ASSISTANCE, AND PROJECT MANAGEMENT FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 STREET RESURFACING PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Approve a Task Order under Willdan
  Engineering’s Master Professional Services Agreement for the 2023-24 Fiscal Year
  Design and Engineering for Street Resurfacing Project, in the amount of $68,671, all
  to the satisfaction of the City Attorney; and 2) Discontinue the “fog seal” application
  on the berms in the Dapplegray neighborhood (currently under construction for this
  year’s re-paving project) in favor of re-paving the berms as part of next fiscal year’s
  re-paving project.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public Works Director Wahba explained that the contractors have come back and corrected
the work identified by staff, in which they will not be paid additionally for, and that the City is still
within the contingency of the approved project budget thus far, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER STEGURA.

Public Works Director Wahba explained that the replacement of the existing center striping was
part of the original plan, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ.

City Manager Grammer explained that the request to not replace the striping by the
neighborhood was expressed after the project was approved. He further explained that going
forward, staff plans to better communicate with the neighborhood Homeowners Associations
(HOAs) prior to finalizing plans and specifications in case any changes are desired.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from Dapplegray Lanes Homeowner Association President
Brian Little and A.J. Poulin.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ emphasized the importance of communicating with HOAs prior
to approving project plans and considering each neighborhood’s aesthetics.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) APPROVE A TASK ORDER UNDER WILLDAN ENGINEERING’S MASTER
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR THE 2023-24 FISCAL YEAR
  DESIGN AND ENGINEERING FOR STREET RESURFACING PROJECT, IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $68,671, ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY
  ATTORNEY; AND 2) DISCONTINUE THE “FOG SEAL” APPLICATION ON
  THE BERMS IN THE DAPPLEGRAY NEIGHBORHOOD (CURRENTLY
  UNDER CONSTRUCTION FOR THIS YEAR’S RE-PAVING PROJECT) IN
  FAVOR OF RE-PAVING THE BERMS AS PART OF NEXT FISCAL YEAR’S
  RE-PAVING PROJECT.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz and Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: ELECTRIC VEHICLE
  CHARGING STATION (EVCS) RATES AT CITY STATIONS

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2541 approving a fee
  structure for public usage of City-owned Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS)
  in the amount of $0.24/ KWh + $0.50 session fee; $2.50 per hour for first 2 hours
  when idle (not charging) with a 20-minute grace period and $5.00 per hour thereafter.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 28, 2023
 Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA, as Chair of the Environmental Advisory Committee,
summarized the discussion and thought process behind the Committee’s recommendation.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2541 APPROVING A FEE STRUCTURE FOR
  PUBLIC USAGE OF CITY-OWNED ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING
  STATIONS (EVCS) IN THE AMOUNT OF $0.24/ KWH + $0.50 SESSION FEE;
  $2.50 PER HOUR FOR FIRST 2 HOURS WHEN IDLE (NOT CHARGING)
  WITH A 20-MINUTE GRACE PERIOD AND $5.00 PER HOUR THEREAFTER.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz and Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2541 by title.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ reported out on the monthly California Contract Cities
Association’s Board meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA attended the South Bay Cities Council of Governments’
Board of Directors meeting.

MAYOR HUFF attended the monthly Peninsula Mayors’ lunch today, as well as the City
Selection Committee meeting yesterday. She also attended the monthly Sanitation District
meeting, as well as the Palos Verdes Chamber of Commerce’s Economic Forecast Breakfast.
Lastly, she attended the Cal Cities’ State Board of Directors meeting. She plans to attend the
rescheduled Little League Opening Day on Saturday.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER met with CalWater representatives to discuss water
conservation measures.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND THE CAL CITIES CITY LEADERS SUMMIT APRIL
  12-14, 2023 IN SACRAMENTO

  CONSENSUS OF COUNCIL TO ALLOW ANY/ALL COUNCIL MEMBERS TO
  ATTEND.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:13 PM MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 28, 2023
 Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 28, 2023
